countries.name: Germany
countries.intro: A country of federal states, old trade cities, forests, rivers, museums, castles, and regional identities that rarely agree with one another.
countries.seo_description: Germany as an editorial travel guide: all sixteen federal states, regional chapters, cities, places, and stories.

countries.name: Austria
countries.intro: A compact Alpine country of imperial cities, mountain valleys, lake regions, music rooms, borderlands, and quietly different provincial identities.
countries.seo_description: Austria as an editorial travel guide: federal states, city chapters, Alpine landscapes, museums, palaces, and places.

regions.name: Baden-Wurttemberg
regions.intro: Black Forest roads, university towns, Swabian kitchens, Lake Constance, and a practical southern confidence.
regions.seo_description: Baden-Wurttemberg as an editorial regional guide: Black Forest, Stuttgart, Heidelberg, Lake Constance, and Swabian culture.

regions.name: Bavaria
regions.intro: Alpine lakes, beer gardens, royal castles, Franconian towns, and a stubborn sense of local identity.
regions.seo_description: Bavaria as an editorial regional guide: Munich, Fussen, Franconia, Alpine lakes, castles, and mountain routes.

regions.name: Berlin
regions.intro: A city-state where the twentieth century remains visible in streets, museums, memorials, clubs, and courtyards.
regions.seo_description: Berlin as an editorial city-state guide: neighbourhoods, museums, memorials, food, nightlife, and urban history.

regions.name: Brandenburg
regions.intro: Lakes, pine forests, palace parks, old garrison towns, and the quieter landscape surrounding Berlin.
regions.seo_description: Brandenburg as an editorial regional guide: Potsdam, lakes, forests, palace parks, and small towns around Berlin.

regions.name: Bremen
regions.intro: A small Hanseatic state of river trade, brick facades, maritime memory, and civic independence.
regions.seo_description: Bremen as an editorial city-state guide: Hanseatic history, river quarters, markets, and maritime culture.

regions.name: Hamburg
regions.intro: A port city-state of warehouses, water, music, merchant money, and northern restraint.
regions.seo_description: Hamburg as an editorial city-state guide: harbour, Speicherstadt, canals, music, food, and northern neighbourhoods.

regions.name: Hesse
regions.intro: Financial towers, spa towns, half-timbered villages, Grimm forests, and vineyard slopes along the Rhine.
regions.seo_description: Hesse as an editorial regional guide: Frankfurt, Wiesbaden, Kassel, Rhine vineyards, and half-timbered towns.

regions.name: Lower Saxony
regions.intro: North Sea islands, heathland, old trading towns, Harz mountains, and a wide northern horizon.
regions.seo_description: Lower Saxony as an editorial regional guide: Hanover, Harz, Luneburg Heath, North Sea coast, and historic towns.

regions.name: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
regions.intro: Baltic islands, chalk cliffs, resort towns, lake country, and a spacious northeastern quiet.
regions.seo_description: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania as an editorial regional guide: Baltic coast, Rugen, Usedom, lake country, and Hanseatic towns.

regions.name: North Rhine-Westphalia
regions.intro: A dense western state of cathedrals, industry, rivers, football cities, museums, and overlapping urban lives.
regions.seo_description: North Rhine-Westphalia as an editorial regional guide: Cologne, Dusseldorf, Ruhr cities, rivers, industry, and museums.

regions.name: Rhineland-Palatinate
regions.intro: Wine valleys, Roman memory, river castles, forest roads, and old towns along the Rhine and Moselle.
regions.seo_description: Rhineland-Palatinate as an editorial regional guide: Rhine, Moselle, Trier, Mainz, wine villages, and castles.

regions.name: Saarland
regions.intro: A compact borderland of industrial memory, French influence, forest walks, and the Saar river bend.
regions.seo_description: Saarland as an editorial regional guide: Saarbrucken, river landscapes, border culture, forests, and industrial heritage.

regions.name: Saxony
regions.intro: Dresden, Leipzig, sandstone cliffs, music history, baroque reconstruction, and a complicated eastern memory.
regions.seo_description: Saxony as an editorial regional guide: Dresden, Leipzig, Saxon Switzerland, music, baroque towns, and eastern history.

regions.name: Saxony-Anhalt
regions.intro: Luther towns, Bauhaus experiments, Romanesque roads, Harz edges, and quiet landscapes with heavy history.
regions.seo_description: Saxony-Anhalt as an editorial regional guide: Magdeburg, Dessau, Wittenberg, Quedlinburg, Bauhaus, and Harz towns.

regions.name: Schleswig-Holstein
regions.intro: Two seas, flat horizons, lighthouses, islands, thatched villages, and northern borderland stories.
regions.seo_description: Schleswig-Holstein as an editorial regional guide: North Sea, Baltic coast, islands, Lubeck, Kiel, and borderland culture.

regions.name: Thuringia
regions.intro: Forest paths, Weimar classicism, Wartburg memory, old university towns, and a compact centre of German culture.
regions.seo_description: Thuringia as an editorial regional guide: Weimar, Erfurt, Jena, Wartburg, Thuringian Forest, and cultural history.

regions.name: Burgenland
regions.intro: Lake light, wine villages, reed landscapes, borderland memory, and a slower eastern edge of Austria.
regions.seo_description: Burgenland as an editorial regional guide: Neusiedler See, wine villages, Esterhazy memory, and eastern Austria.

regions.name: Carinthia
regions.intro: Southern lakes, mountain roads, Slovenian edges, warm summers, and a softer Alpine rhythm.
regions.seo_description: Carinthia as an editorial regional guide: lakes, Klagenfurt, Alpine routes, and southern Austrian culture.

regions.name: Lower Austria
regions.intro: Vineyard valleys, abbeys, Danube routes, old market towns, and the wide country around Vienna.
regions.seo_description: Lower Austria as an editorial regional guide: Wachau, St. Polten, abbeys, Danube towns, and wine landscapes.

regions.name: Upper Austria
regions.intro: Danube industry, lake country, baroque monasteries, salt landscapes, and a practical central Austrian weight.
regions.seo_description: Upper Austria as an editorial regional guide: Linz, Salzkammergut, Danube routes, monasteries, and lakes.

regions.name: Salzburg
regions.intro: A compact state of music, baroque city views, lake districts, Alpine valleys, and polished mountain theatre.
regions.seo_description: Salzburg as an editorial regional guide: Salzburg city, lakes, Alpine valleys, music, and baroque streets.

regions.name: Styria
regions.intro: Green hills, Graz courtyards, wine roads, thermal towns, and a generous southeastern texture.
regions.seo_description: Styria as an editorial regional guide: Graz, wine roads, thermal landscapes, hills, and southeastern Austria.

regions.name: Tyrol
regions.intro: High valleys, passes, mountain towns, ski culture, painted facades, and a strong Alpine identity.
regions.seo_description: Tyrol as an editorial regional guide: Innsbruck, Alpine valleys, passes, villages, and mountain culture.

regions.name: Vorarlberg
regions.intro: Western lake edges, timber architecture, Swiss-facing habits, mountain villages, and compact design culture.
regions.seo_description: Vorarlberg as an editorial regional guide: Bregenz, Lake Constance, mountain villages, timber architecture, and western Austria.

regions.name: Vienna
regions.intro: A federal city-state of palaces, museums, coffeehouses, imperial ceremony, social housing, and daily urban theatre.
regions.seo_description: Vienna as an editorial city-state guide: palaces, museums, coffeehouses, music, urban history, and districts.

cities.name: Stuttgart
cities.intro: A car-industry capital set between hills, vineyards, museums, and Swabian practicality.
cities.seo_description: Stuttgart as an editorial city guide: museums, vineyards, architecture, food, and Baden-Wurttemberg context.

cities.name: Munich
cities.intro: The Bavarian capital reads best as museums, beer gardens, public squares, neighbourhoods, and day trips.
cities.seo_description: Munich as an editorial city guide with neighbourhoods, museums, beer gardens, squares, and day trips.

cities.name: Berlin
cities.intro: A capital and city-state where history, food, nightlife, museums, and neighbourhood life overlap.
cities.seo_description: Berlin as an editorial city guide: neighbourhoods, museums, memorials, food, and urban history.

cities.name: Potsdam
cities.intro: A palace city beside Berlin, built from parks, lakes, Prussian memory, and quiet streets.
cities.seo_description: Potsdam as an editorial city guide: Sanssouci, palace parks, lakes, and Prussian history.

cities.name: Bremen
cities.intro: A Hanseatic river city of brick facades, market squares, maritime memory, and civic independence.
cities.seo_description: Bremen as an editorial city guide: market square, Schnoor, river, Hanseatic history, and maritime culture.

cities.name: Hamburg
cities.intro: A port city of warehouses, canals, music, merchant money, and northern restraint.
cities.seo_description: Hamburg as an editorial city guide: harbour, Speicherstadt, canals, music, food, and northern neighbourhoods.

cities.name: Wiesbaden
cities.intro: A spa capital of warm springs, villas, theatre, hills, and Rhine-side elegance.
cities.seo_description: Wiesbaden as an editorial city guide: spa architecture, thermal springs, villas, and Rhine context.

cities.name: Hanover
cities.intro: A northern state capital of gardens, trade fairs, rebuilt streets, and access to wider Lower Saxony.
cities.seo_description: Hanover as an editorial city guide: Herrenhausen Gardens, museums, trade-fair city, and Lower Saxony context.

cities.name: Schwerin
cities.intro: A small lake capital built around a theatrical castle, old streets, and northern water light.
cities.seo_description: Schwerin as an editorial city guide: castle, lake landscape, old town, and Mecklenburg context.

cities.name: Dusseldorf
cities.intro: A Rhine-side capital of art, fashion, business, Altbier, and a compact old town.
cities.seo_description: Dusseldorf as an editorial city guide: Rhine promenade, art museums, Altstadt, fashion, and NRW context.

cities.name: Mainz
cities.intro: A Rhine city of Roman memory, printing history, wine culture, and cathedral streets.
cities.seo_description: Mainz as an editorial city guide: cathedral, Gutenberg, Roman history, wine, and Rhine context.

cities.name: Saarbrucken
cities.intro: A borderland capital shaped by the Saar, French influence, industrial memory, and relaxed street life.
cities.seo_description: Saarbrucken as an editorial city guide: Saar river, border culture, food, and industrial heritage.

cities.name: Dresden
cities.intro: A baroque river city of reconstruction, museums, music, memory, and sandstone horizons nearby.
cities.seo_description: Dresden as an editorial city guide: old town, museums, Elbe, reconstruction, and Saxon context.

cities.name: Magdeburg
cities.intro: An Elbe city of cathedral memory, modern rebuilding, Romanesque routes, and central German weight.
cities.seo_description: Magdeburg as an editorial city guide: cathedral, Elbe, Romanesque history, and Saxony-Anhalt context.

cities.name: Kiel
cities.intro: A Baltic port capital of ferries, sailing, naval history, and northern sea air.
cities.seo_description: Kiel as an editorial city guide: Baltic port, sailing, ferries, naval history, and Schleswig-Holstein context.

cities.name: Erfurt
cities.intro: A compact old city of bridges, cathedral steps, medieval streets, and Thuringian centre of gravity.
cities.seo_description: Erfurt as an editorial city guide: cathedral, Kramerbrucke, old town, and Thuringian context.

cities.name: Eisenstadt
cities.intro: A small capital shaped by Esterhazy memory, wine country, and the open eastern edge of Austria.
cities.seo_description: Eisenstadt as an editorial city guide: Esterhazy Palace, wine country, and Burgenland context.

cities.name: Klagenfurt
cities.intro: A southern lake capital of courtyards, warm summers, bilingual edges, and access to Carinthian water landscapes.
cities.seo_description: Klagenfurt as an editorial city guide: old town, Worthersee, southern Austria, and Carinthia context.

cities.name: St. Polten
cities.intro: A modern state capital set near older Danube routes, abbeys, vineyards, and Lower Austrian market towns.
cities.seo_description: St. Polten as an editorial city guide: Lower Austria, Danube routes, abbeys, and regional context.

cities.name: Linz
cities.intro: A Danube city where industry, media art, baroque streets, and central Austrian practicality meet.
cities.seo_description: Linz as an editorial city guide: Danube, Ars Electronica, old town, industry, and Upper Austria context.

cities.name: Salzburg
cities.intro: A baroque city of music, fortress views, river walks, festival memory, and Alpine proximity.
cities.seo_description: Salzburg as an editorial city guide: old town, fortress, music, river views, and Alpine context.

cities.name: Graz
cities.intro: A courtyard city of red roofs, university life, design culture, food markets, and Styrian hills nearby.
cities.seo_description: Graz as an editorial city guide: old town, Schlossberg, courtyards, design, food, and Styria context.

cities.name: Innsbruck
cities.intro: An Alpine city where imperial streets sit directly beneath high mountains and valley routes.
cities.seo_description: Innsbruck as an editorial city guide: old town, mountains, imperial memory, and Tyrol context.

cities.name: Bregenz
cities.intro: A Lake Constance city of festival stages, mountain lifts, timber design, and western Austrian edges.
cities.seo_description: Bregenz as an editorial city guide: Lake Constance, Pfander, festival culture, and Vorarlberg context.

cities.name: Vienna
cities.intro: A capital of palaces, museums, coffeehouses, public housing, music rooms, and district-by-district urban life.
cities.seo_description: Vienna as an editorial city guide: palaces, museums, coffeehouses, music, and urban history.

places.name: Mercedes-Benz Museum
places.intro: A spiral museum of engineering, industry, speed, and modern German manufacturing memory.
places.long_form_story: The Mercedes-Benz Museum turns car history into a social and industrial timeline, useful even for visitors who are not interested in engines.
places.seasonality_text: A reliable indoor anchor in any season.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart.

places.name: Marienplatz
places.intro: Munich's civic heart since 1158, anchored by the New Town Hall and its daily Glockenspiel.
places.long_form_story: Marienplatz has been market, ceremonial ground, transport node, and default meeting place for nine centuries.
places.seasonality_text: Early morning is the calmest time. December brings Christmas market crowds.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Marienplatz in Munich.

places.name: Museum Island
places.intro: A cluster of major museums on the Spree, where empire, archaeology, art, and reconstruction meet.
places.long_form_story: Museum Island is less a single sight than a concentrated argument about collections, architecture, restoration, and cultural power.
places.seasonality_text: Book timed tickets for major museums and leave more time than expected.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Museum Island in Berlin.

places.name: Sanssouci Park
places.intro: A palace landscape of terraces, long views, Prussian theatre, and carefully staged leisure.
places.long_form_story: Sanssouci is best read as a park before it is read as a palace: movement, gardens, architecture, and power arranged as scenery.
places.seasonality_text: Gardens carry the visit; spring and autumn are especially good.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Sanssouci Park in Potsdam.

places.name: Bremen Market Square
places.intro: A compact civic stage framed by Hanseatic facades, the town hall, Roland, and merchant memory.
places.long_form_story: Bremen's market square is the clearest way to understand the city's old independence and merchant self-image.
places.seasonality_text: December adds Christmas market crowds and atmosphere.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Bremen Market Square.

places.name: Speicherstadt
places.intro: A warehouse district of brick, canals, bridges, trade memory, and modern reuse.
places.long_form_story: Speicherstadt is Hamburg's merchant history made walkable: red brick, water, storage, customs, and the afterlife of port architecture.
places.seasonality_text: Evening light and wet weather both suit the brick and canals.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Speicherstadt in Hamburg.

places.name: Kurhaus Wiesbaden
places.intro: A spa-era landmark of columns, ceremony, gambling rooms, and cultivated civic elegance.
places.long_form_story: The Kurhaus gives Wiesbaden its clearest architectural statement: a city built around health, display, and respectable leisure.
places.seasonality_text: Works in all seasons, especially as part of a slow walk through the spa district.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Kurhaus in Wiesbaden.

places.name: Herrenhausen Gardens
places.intro: A formal garden landscape where Hanover keeps its courtly memory visible.
places.long_form_story: Herrenhausen Gardens give Hanover a more graceful first impression than the rebuilt centre: geometry, fountains, old court taste, and seasonal walking.
places.seasonality_text: Best when the gardens are in full seasonal use.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Herrenhausen Gardens in Hanover.

places.name: Schwerin Castle
places.intro: A theatrical castle set on an island, reflected in lake water and northern light.
places.long_form_story: Schwerin Castle is both seat of parliament and fairy-tale image, a useful contradiction for understanding Mecklenburg's capital.
places.seasonality_text: Best when the park and lake walks are part of the visit.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Schwerin Castle.

places.name: Rhine Promenade
places.intro: A riverside walk that turns Dusseldorf toward the water and links old town, art, bridges, and city life.
places.long_form_story: The Rhine Promenade is the easiest way to read Dusseldorf's balance of business, art, old-town sociability, and river-facing confidence.
places.seasonality_text: Best in late afternoon and evening.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Rhine Promenade in Dusseldorf.

places.name: Mainz Cathedral
places.intro: A heavy Romanesque cathedral at the centre of a Rhine city shaped by bishops, printers, and wine.
places.long_form_story: Mainz Cathedral gives the city its gravity: stone, power, ceremony, and a long Rhine history gathered into one square.
places.seasonality_text: Pair with old-town lanes and the Gutenberg Museum.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Mainz Cathedral.

places.name: Saarbrucken Castle
places.intro: A rebuilt castle above the Saar, useful for reading the city's borderland layers.
places.long_form_story: Saarbrucken Castle is less about medieval romance than the layered identity of a city between German and French influences.
places.seasonality_text: Works as part of a compact city walk.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Saarbrucken Castle.

places.name: Zwinger
places.intro: A baroque palace complex where Dresden performs splendour, reconstruction, and museum culture.
places.long_form_story: The Zwinger is not only ornament. It is Dresden's theatrical memory of court culture and the city's determination to rebuild beauty after destruction.
places.seasonality_text: Courtyards are best in good weather; museums carry rainy days.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Zwinger in Dresden.

places.name: Magdeburg Cathedral
places.intro: A Gothic cathedral on the Elbe, tied to imperial memory and the city's long rebuildings.
places.long_form_story: Magdeburg Cathedral gives the city its deepest historical register: empire, religion, destruction, rebuilding, and the long line of central German memory.
places.seasonality_text: Works in any season and pairs with an Elbe walk.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Magdeburg Cathedral.

places.name: Kiel Fjord
places.intro: A working Baltic waterway of ferries, sailing, naval memory, and northern light.
places.long_form_story: Kiel is best understood from the water. The fjord explains the city's scale, history, and daily orientation better than any single monument.
places.seasonality_text: Best in sailing season, especially around long summer evenings.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Kiel Fjord.

places.name: Kramerbrucke
places.intro: A medieval bridge lined with houses, still carrying shops, pedestrians, and Erfurt's old-town identity.
places.long_form_story: Kramerbrucke is small enough to cross quickly and rich enough to define the city's image: trade, craft, continuity, and lived medieval fabric.
places.seasonality_text: Best early or late before the bridge becomes crowded.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Kramerbrucke in Erfurt.

places.name: Esterhazy Palace
places.intro: A princely palace that gives Eisenstadt its clearest architectural and musical centre.
places.long_form_story: Esterhazy Palace is the quickest way to understand Eisenstadt: court culture, Haydn memory, regional pride, and wine country gathered into one landmark.
places.seasonality_text: Works in any season and pairs naturally with Burgenland wine routes.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Esterhazy Palace in Eisenstadt.

places.name: Worthersee
places.intro: A warm southern lake that shapes Klagenfurt's summer rhythm and Carinthia's relaxed image.
places.long_form_story: Worthersee is less a single sight than a seasonal mood: lake light, swimming platforms, villas, boat routes, and an Austrian south that feels softer than the high Alps.
places.seasonality_text: Best from late spring through early autumn.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Worthersee near Klagenfurt.

places.name: Wachau Valley
places.intro: A Danube landscape of vineyards, abbeys, river towns, and slow Austrian travel.
places.long_form_story: The Wachau Valley is one of Lower Austria's best entry points: wine terraces, Melk Abbey, small towns, river movement, and a landscape built for unhurried routes.
places.seasonality_text: Best when vineyards and river routes are part of the day.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Wachau Valley in Lower Austria.

places.name: Ars Electronica Center
places.intro: A media-art landmark that gives Linz a sharper contemporary edge beside the Danube.
places.long_form_story: The Ars Electronica Center helps explain modern Linz: not only baroque streets and industry, but technology, art, education, and public experimentation on the river.
places.seasonality_text: A reliable indoor anchor in any season.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Ars Electronica Center in Linz.

places.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
places.intro: A hilltop fortress that turns Salzburg's baroque old town and Alpine edge into one view.
places.long_form_story: Hohensalzburg Fortress is Salzburg's clearest vertical landmark: defensive history, prince-archbishop power, old-town theatre, and mountain horizon in a single climb.
places.seasonality_text: Clear days make the view do most of the work.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Hohensalzburg Fortress in Salzburg.

places.name: Schlossberg
places.intro: A hill above Graz where clocktower, views, paths, and red roofs explain the city at once.
places.long_form_story: Schlossberg is the easiest way to read Graz: old town below, courtyards hidden in the grid, hills around the city, and a landmark that is both viewpoint and memory.
places.seasonality_text: Best at golden hour and in mild weather.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Schlossberg in Graz.

places.name: Golden Roof
places.intro: A small imperial landmark that anchors Innsbruck's old town beneath the mountains.
places.long_form_story: The Golden Roof is compact but useful: Maximilian memory, painted facades, old-town theatre, and the sudden presence of high mountains above the street.
places.seasonality_text: Works in any season as part of an old-town walk.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to the Golden Roof in Innsbruck.

places.name: Pfander
places.intro: A mountain above Bregenz with Lake Constance views and a clean western Austrian horizon.
places.long_form_story: Pfander gives Bregenz its vertical escape: lake below, Switzerland and Germany nearby, mountain paths above, and a compact sense of Vorarlberg's borderland geography.
places.seasonality_text: Best with clear weather for lake and mountain views.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Pfander above Bregenz.

places.name: Schonbrunn Palace
places.intro: An imperial palace landscape that turns Vienna's monarchy, gardens, and visitor rituals into one route.
places.long_form_story: Schonbrunn Palace is one of Vienna's clearest large-scale entries: rooms, gardens, hill views, imperial choreography, and the question of how a capital performs memory.
places.seasonality_text: Gardens are strongest from spring through autumn; interiors carry winter.
places.seo_description: A short editorial guide to Schonbrunn Palace in Vienna.
